Implementation Plan

**Implementation plan: issue #6434, push guard checks the raw remote URL instead of the URL Git will actually push to**

Refs #3576 (tracking issue for the security audit; do not use an auto-close keyword for it).

Planning ref: `git rev-parse HEAD` = `d071be9ae998e9c8c48be1072e26839ce0867b07`, branch `claude/replace-claude-sessions-phase-5d`. This matches the issue's integration branch, so there is no mismatch.

Scope-mode: Hold Scope
Reuse-audit: extends `_resolve_push_destination`
Scope-mode justification: The finding is about one function. `_resolve_push_destination` and `_remote_push_urls` (around lines 812–853 of `.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py`) read `remote.<name>.pushurl` / `remote.<name>.url` with plain `git config --get-all` and never apply `url.*.insteadOf` / `url.*.pushInsteadOf`. The command parser `_guarded_git_invocations` also skips `-c` and drops every prefix assignment except `GIT_DIR` / `GIT_WORK_TREE`. The fix extends those two existing functions and the NamedTuples they fill. It adds no new script, workflow, scheduler hook or dependency. Following Boil the Lake (complete fix ≤30 LOC more than the shortcut, no new dependency or interface), the plan also covers the sibling bypasses that cost a few lines each and are the same defect class: rewrites already in persistent config, the `GIT_CONFIG_*` environment, `-c remote.<name>.pushurl` and `-c remote.pushDefault`, and the `env VAR=… git push` wrapper. Without them the same disclosure stays open. This follows §6: Security > Correctness & safety > Backward compatibility > Operational clarity > Performance > Speed.

**Automation / §20 surface**
- Only modifies existing code: the hook and its byte-identical template twin, plus tests, a changelog fragment and one `agents.md` sentence.
- No scheduler or PR-push entry point changes. The hook is already registered as a PreToolUse hook in `.claude/settings.json` and `workflow-templates/.claude/settings.json`; neither changes.
- No long-running supervisor, no DB work, no `docs/scripts-pending-removal.md` entry.

**Verified facts (git 2.55.0, checked in a scratch repo)**
- `git config --get remote.origin.url` returns the raw URL. `git -c url.https://evil.example/.pushInsteadOf=https://x-access-token:SECRET@github.com/ remote get-url --push --all origin` returns `https://evil.example/o/r.git`. This is the bypass the finding describes, and the token prefix is what gets rewritten.
- `-c …insteadOf=` and the `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT` / `GIT_CONFIG_KEY_n` / `GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_n` environment variables are honoured by `remote get-url --push` in the same way.
- An explicit `pushurl` ignores `pushInsteadOf` but is still rewritten by `insteadOf`. When several rules match, the longest prefix wins. `remote get-url --push` already implements all of this.
- `remote get-url` refuses remotes that are not configured: `-c remote.zzprobe.url=…` gives "No such remote". So a literal-URL push (`git push https://…`) cannot be resolved by Git directly. It needs a Python port of git's `alias_url` rule, fed from `git config -z --get-regexp '^url\..*\.(pushinsteadof|insteadof)$'`, which does honour `-c`, the environment and includes.
- An identity rule (`url.https://github.com/o/r.git.pushInsteadOf=https://github.com/o/r.git`) keeps the push URL on GitHub while `insteadOf` still sends fetch/ls-remote to a local bare repo. The test fixtures need this (see Risks).
- With `remote.origin.pushurl=""`, git ≥2.46 `get-url --push` returns the fetch URL. The existing test `test_empty_pushurl_is_not_treated_as_fetch_url` expects a block, so the raw-config check stays in place as a fail-closed pre-check.

**1. Files likely to change**
- `.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py`
- `workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py` (must stay byte-identical; currently identical, 1678 lines each)
- `tests/test_pr_merge_status_guard.py` (new tests, plus fixture updates in `merge_commit_repo` around line 1761 and `test_history_fallback_uses_push_destination_remote` around line 1878, the 3 `insteadOf` uses)
- `changelog.d/6434-push-guard-effective-push-url.md` (new)
- `agents.md`: one sentence next to the existing "merged-PR push guard" note

**2. Functions / modules to implement or change (in `pr_merge_status_guard.py`)**
- **New constants:**
  - `_GIT_CONFIG_ENV_RE`, matching `GIT_CONFIG`, `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT`, `GIT_CONFIG_KEY_<n>`, `GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_<n>`, `GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS`, `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL`, `GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM`, `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM`, `HOME`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`.
  - `_RESOLVE_ENV`: `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`, `GIT_PAGER=cat`, `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0`.
  - Grep before adding to make sure neither name collides with an existing one (§10).
- **`_GitInvocation` and `_GuardTarget`:** add trailing defaulted fields so existing positional construction keeps working:
  - `config_args: tuple[str, ...] = ()`, the flattened `("-c", "k=v", …)`.
  - `config_environment: tuple[tuple[str, str], ...] = ()`.
  - `config_uncertain: str = ""`, a reason string.
- **`_guarded_git_invocations`:**
  - Prefix assignments whose name matches `_GIT_CONFIG_ENV_RE` go into `config_environment`. They must not go into `environment`, so they are never path-resolved by `_literal_guard_path` and never reach the hook's network calls. A `NAME+=` form on such a name sets `config_uncertain`.
  - In the global-option loop:
    - `-c <value>` is recorded in `config_args`.
    - `--config-env…` sets `config_uncertain` ("git --config-env reads a variable the guard cannot see").
    - A `-c` value or config-env value containing `$` or a backtick sets `config_uncertain`.
  - Command-level state carried across segments sets `config_uncertain` for every later push in the same command when an earlier segment:
    - is a `git` invocation with subcommand `config` (other than the `--get*`, `-l`, `--list` or `--show-*` read forms) or `remote` (other than `get-url`, `show`, `-v` or bare); or
    - is `export`, `declare`, `typeset`, `readonly`, `unset` or an assignment-only segment that names a config-affecting variable.

    The hook runs before the command, so config the command writes itself cannot be resolved ahead of time. This check sits before the existing `tokens[index] not in GUARDED_SUBCOMMANDS: continue`.
  - `env` wrapper: when the command word is `env`, skip it. Its `NAME=value` arguments are handled like prefix assignments. Any `env` option (`-i`, `-u`, `-S`, `--…`) sets `config_uncertain`.
- **`git_subcommands`:** the same `env [NAME=value…] [options] git …` recognition, so `env GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=… git push` is no longer invisible to the guard. Update the docstring: `env` is now recognised; `sudo` and other wrappers still are not.
- **`_push_targets`:** copy `config_args`, `config_environment` and `config_uncertain` from the invocation onto every `_GuardTarget` it builds.
- **New `_inline_git_config(config_args, config_environment)` context helper:** wraps `_git_environment` with `{**current overrides, **config_environment, **_RESOLVE_ENV}`. Resolution commands become `["git", "--no-pager", *config_args, …]`. It is used only by the local-only helpers below and never by `default_branch`, `fetch_from_origin`, `remote_branch_tip`, `ls-remote` or `query_pull_requests`.
- **New `_effective_remote_push_urls(name, cwd, config_args)`:**
  - runs `git --no-pager <config_args> remote get-url --push --all <name>` under the inline config;
  - returns `list[str]`, or `None` on a non-zero exit;
  - the name has already been validated by `_REMOTE_NAME_RE`, which cannot start with `-`.
- **New `_url_rewrite_rules(cwd, config_args)`:**
  - runs `git --no-pager <config_args> config -z --get-regexp '^url\..*\.(pushinsteadof|insteadof)$'`;
  - exit 1 means no rules;
  - other non-zero exits mean `None` (fail closed);
  - parses NUL-separated `key\nvalue` entries in config order;
  - returns two lists of `(value_prefix, base)`, one for push rules and one for fetch rules.
- **New `_rewrite_push_url(url, rules)`:** port of git `remote.c` `alias_url`:
  - the longest matching `pushInsteadOf` prefix on the original URL wins, and the first-defined rule wins a tie (strictly-greater comparison);
  - if no push rule matches, the longest matching `insteadOf` prefix applies;
  - otherwise the URL is unchanged.
- **`_default_push_remote(cwd)`:** gains an optional `config_args=()` parameter and runs its `git config --get` reads under the inline config, so `-c remote.pushDefault=…` and `-c branch.<b>.pushRemote=…` are honoured.
- **`_resolve_push_destination(cwd, push_repository, config_args=(), config_environment=())`:**
  - Configured-remote branch:
    - The existing raw check stays, but its config reads now run under the inline config. A raw non-GitHub or empty entry still fails as before.
    - Then call `_effective_remote_push_urls`. `None` gives failure "could not resolve the effective push URL".
    - Any effective URL for which `extract_repo_slug` returns "" gives failure "a url.*.insteadOf/pushInsteadOf rewrite sends the push to a non-GitHub destination".
    - `slugs` come from the effective URLs.
    - `history_remote` is kept only when no inline config is present and the existing fetch-URL comparison matches the effective slugs. Otherwise it is "": the hook's own fetch runs without the command's config, so it could inspect a different repository.
  - Literal-URL branch:
    - The raw URL must map to GitHub, as today.
    - Then apply `_rewrite_push_url` with `_url_rewrite_rules`. `None` rules give a failure.
    - The rewritten URL must also map, and the slug comes from the rewritten URL.
  - The failure text never includes an effective URL. `label` keeps its existing userinfo redaction.
- **`_evaluate_bash`:**
  - A target with `config_uncertain` is treated like the existing "could not resolve git push" path: its reason goes into `unknown_destination_reasons`, which leads to `_request_confirmation`.
